source.title: Generalization Error Bounds of Gradient Descent for Learning Over-Parameterized Deep ReLU Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results about gradient descent training deep ReLU networks from random initialization, using surrogate training error and population classification error under specified data assumptions. It does not run the benchmark experiments named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds, not CIFAR benchmarks or empirical training runs. Its related-work discussion of fitting random labels and cited convergence results is not recorded as this paper's result.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional optimization and generalization guarantees for fully connected binary ReLU networks. These results do not test the specified convolutional benchmark claim, teacher–student minima frequencies, or comparisons involving depth, initialization, stability thresholds, or normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under specified data-distribution assumptions and sufficient width and sample size, gradient descent with the prescribed Gaussian initialization and step size achieves arbitrarily small population classification error for fully connected deep ReLU binary classifiers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes fully connected binary ReLU networks trained with full-batch gradient descent and cross-entropy from He-style Gaussian initialization. It gives theoretical guarantees under separability assumptions rather than the benchmark training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on data separability assumptions, network depth, width, sample size, initialization neighborhood, and step size.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.7 guarantees arbitrarily small empirical surrogate error near Gaussian initialization under a gradient lower bound and sufficient width. This also implies arbitrarily small training classification error in this fully connected setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide fully connected deep ReLU networks trained by full-batch gradient descent from He-style Gaussian initialization achieve arbitrarily small training classification error under the stated gradient lower-bound condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Under random-feature or conjugate-kernel margin separability, sufficient width and sample size yield arbitrarily small population classification error. Theorem 4.5 supplies a uniform generalization bound near initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the specified separability assumptions, gradient descent on sufficiently wide fully connected deep ReLU networks generalizes with arbitrarily small population classification error.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and conditional on stated assumptions; no benchmark training runs or empirical CIFAR results are reported. The paper notes that a generic pairwise-separation condition can yield a vacuous population-error bound when labels are independent of inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results were left out; the cited prior-work findings and related-work discussion are not rows.

untested.parts: SGD or Adam training of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and the stated model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher–student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two additional student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization recipes.
Effects of initialization choice on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth. He initialization is used without a comparison.
Training above stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Normalization comparisons, acceleration, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical results can test a claim, but these results do not match any version in play. Citations about fitting random labels and avoiding spurious minima are prior work, not this study's findings. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes; the paper studies fully connected binary classifiers under separability assumptions and does not report empirical training classification error.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual architectures, depth-related training degradation, and shortcut comparisons.
Comparisons among initializations, training speed, or trainable depth; Gaussian He initialization is specified but not compared.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises or divergence, and sharpness dynamics.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed, and learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: deep fully connected ReLU network trained by Algorithm 1
rows.size_stated: L hidden layers; layer widths m_l with balanced widths; sufficient m as specified in Theorem 4.7
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on cross-entropy from independent Gaussian initialization N(0, 2/m_l) for each weight entry; theorem guarantees an iterate with empirical surrogate error at most ε under the stated gradient lower bound.

conditions.value: n training examples drawn independently from fixed binary classification distribution
Gaussian N(0, 2/m_l), identified as He initialization
gradient lower bound (4.1) holds throughout the initialization neighborhood

rows.value: E_S(W^(k)) ≤ ε for some iterate among K = O(L^3 B^-4 ε^-2) iterations
rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ, for the stated sufficient width; ε, δ > 0.
rows.note: The result is a theoretical guarantee for surrogate error; it is not a reported CIFAR training classification error.
rows.check: A valid conditional theorem, but outside all six versions. Small empirical surrogate error also bounds training classification error by 2ε; the mismatch with V1 is the architecture, setting, and training algorithm, rather than surrogate error alone. The iteration bound uses Õ, not O.

rows.subject: deep fully connected ReLU network trained by Algorithm 1
rows.size_stated: L hidden layers; width and sample size at least the stated m*(ε,L,γ,δ) and n*(ε,L,γ,δ)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on cross-entropy from Gaussian initialization under separability by a random ReLU feature; reports a population classification error guarantee.

conditions.value: Assumption 4.10: separable by random ReLU feature with margin γ

rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ; m* = Õ(poly(2^L, γ^-1)) · ε^-14 · log(1/δ), n* = Õ(poly(2^L, γ^-1)) · ε^-4 · log(1/δ); K = Õ(poly(2^L, γ^-1)) · ε^-2 iterations.
rows.note: This is a population-error theorem under the specified margin-separability assumption, not a CIFAR experiment.
rows.check: The population-error guarantee does not measure any listed version. Corollary 4.11 guarantees P(yf(x) > 0) ≥ 1−ε, equivalently P(yf(x) ≤ 0) ≤ ε; the recorded strict-negative error bound is valid but weaker.

rows.subject: deep fully connected ReLU network trained by Algorithm 1
rows.size_stated: L hidden layers; width and sample size at least the stated m*(ε,L,γ,δ) and n*(ε,L,γ,δ)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on cross-entropy from Gaussian initialization under conjugate-kernel separability; reports a population classification error guarantee.

conditions.value: Assumption 4.12: separable by the conjugate kernel with RKHS norm at most 1 and margin γ

rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ; m* = Õ(poly(L, γ^-1)) · ε^-14 · log(1/δ), n* = Õ(poly(L, γ^-1)) · ε^-4 · log(1/δ); K = Õ(poly(γ^-1)) · ε^-2 iterations.
rows.note: This is a population-error theorem under the specified conjugate-kernel separability assumption, not a benchmark experiment.
rows.check: The population-error guarantee does not measure any listed version. Corollary 4.13 guarantees P(yf(x) > 0) ≥ 1−ε, equivalently P(yf(x) ≤ 0) ≤ ε; the recorded strict-negative error bound is valid but weaker.

rows.subject: deep fully connected ReLU network with parameters in the initialization neighborhood
rows.size_stated: L hidden layers; width m and neighborhood radius τ subject to Theorem 4.5
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical uniform bound relating population classification error to empirical surrogate error over a neighborhood of Gaussian initialization.

conditions.value: n training examples from the fixed binary classification distribution

rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ under Theorem 4.5's width and neighborhood conditions.
rows.note: A bound conditional on empirical surrogate error; it does not independently report a measured training result.
rows.check: This conditional generalization bound is outside all six versions. Correct its middle term to C Lτ√(m/n), as confirmed by the proof in Section 5.1, rather than C√(Lτ)√(m/n).
